versions.question: A team wants to describe its VPC, subnets and EC2 instances in a file and have AWS build them in a sensible order. Which service fits?
versions.explanation: CloudFormation reads the template and works out how to create everything.
option_explanations: Records resource configuration; it doesn't create resources.

versions.question: Writing a CloudFormation template, what can the author leave for the service to work out?
versions.explanation: Declarative: you say what you want, CloudFormation decides how and in which order.
option_explanations: Correct. CloudFormation derives it from dependencies.

versions.question: Which are advantages of managing infrastructure through CloudFormation templates? (Choose 3)
options: EC2 instances stop needing IAM roles
Every infrastructure change is versioned like code
Tagging by stack makes spend easy to follow
Applications get compiled and hosted by it
A dev setup can be torn down at night and rebuilt
versions.explanation: Other benefits: automatic diagrams, separation of concerns and template reuse.
option_explanations: Instances still need roles for their own AWS calls.
Correct. No manual creation; review through version control.
Correct. Costs per stack are visible and estimable.
It provisions infrastructure, not app hosting.
Correct. Saves money outside working hours.

versions.question: Which is a real way CloudFormation helps cut AWS costs?
options: Its resources are billed at a lower rate
Its stacks get an EC2 pricing discount
Stacks can be deleted and rebuilt on demand
versions.explanation: Deleting and recreating environments from the same template is a common cost saver.
option_explanations: Resources cost the same however they're created.
Stacks don't pause anything on their own.
Correct. The template recreates the environment in the morning.

versions.question: A stack is running and its template needs a change. What's the supported way to apply it?
options: Update the stack with a revised template
Create a second stack with the same name
versions.explanation: Updating a stack applies a new template version to the same stack.
option_explanations: Correct. Upload the new version and update.
Stack names must be unique in a Region.

versions.question: What identifies a CloudFormation stack, so an update targets the right one?
versions.explanation: Stacks are identified by name within a Region.
option_explanations: Many stacks can share a bucket.

versions.question: A developer deletes a stack that created an SQS queue and an EC2 instance, with no DeletionPolicy set. What happens to them?
options: They're kept and need manual cleanup
versions.explanation: Deleting a stack deletes what it created, unless a DeletionPolicy says otherwise.
option_explanations: Correct. CloudFormation deletes them in the right order.

versions.question: Which setting keeps a resource when its stack is deleted?
versions.explanation: Without a DeletionPolicy, deleting a stack removes everything it created.
option_explanations: Applies to replacements during updates, and Delete removes it.
Stack policies guard updates, not deletes.
Correct. Snapshot also works for some types.

versions.question: Which are two common ways to get a CloudFormation template deployed? (Choose 2)
options: Run it from a CI/CD pipeline or the AWS CLI
Attach it to an EC2 instance as user data
Drop it into an S3 bucket to trigger a deploy
Upload it in the console after editing locally
versions.explanation: Templates are usually YAML files kept in version control.
option_explanations: User data runs on one instance; it doesn't create stacks.

versions.question: A team wants every template change deployed automatically, with no console clicks. What fits?
versions.explanation: Automated deployment: template files plus the CLI or a CI/CD tool.
option_explanations: A visual editor; deploying from it is manual.
Correct. It runs the CLI or deploy action on each change.

versions.question: A template has only a Resources section. Is it valid?
options: No; a format version is also required
Yes; no other section is required
versions.explanation: Resources is the one mandatory section.

versions.question: Which template section can't be left out?
versions.explanation: Everything else, including Parameters and Description, is optional.

versions.question: Which template section decides whether a resource or output gets created?
versions.explanation: Conditions are true/false checks applied to resources or outputs.

versions.question: In a template, what's the Outputs section for?
options: Fixed lookup tables keyed by Region
Values you view or share with other stacks
Values users type in when deploying the stack
The AWS resources the stack builds
versions.explanation: Parameters are inputs, Mappings are static lookups, Outputs are values to view or export.

versions.question: In a CloudFormation YAML template, what do lines starting with `- ` under a key create?
versions.explanation: Indentation nests objects; `-` items form a list.
option_explanations: Correct. Each `-` line is one item.
Indented `key: value` lines make a map.

versions.question: In YAML, which character starts a comment?
versions.explanation: Everything after `#` on a line is ignored.

versions.question: Which is a correctly formed CloudFormation resource type?
versions.explanation: Format: service-provider::service-name::data-type-name.

versions.question: In `AWS::DynamoDB::Table`, what does the middle part name?
versions.explanation: Each type's properties are listed in the CloudFormation docs.

versions.question: A stack update changes a property documented as 'Replacement'. What does CloudFormation do?
options: A new resource takes its place
versions.explanation: Each property documents its update behavior: no interruption, some interruption or replacement.
option_explanations: Correct. The new one gets a new physical ID.

versions.question: Changing an EC2 instance's ImageId in a stack update leads to what?
options: The new AMI is applied in place
versions.explanation: Check the docs' update behavior before changing a property.
option_explanations: An AMI can't be swapped in place.

versions.question: Which CloudFormation feature previews an update, including whether each resource will be swapped out?
versions.explanation: Review a change set before executing it.
option_explanations: Compares live resources to the template.

versions.question: A change set entry shows `Replacement: True`. What does that mean?
versions.explanation: Change sets list each add, modify or remove and whether it replaces the resource.
option_explanations: Correct. It's recreated, then the old one deleted.

versions.question: A team needs CloudFormation to manage something no built-in resource type covers. What should they add?
versions.explanation: Custom resources fill gaps in CloudFormation support.

versions.question: Which situation calls for a CloudFormation custom resource?
options: Creating many similar resources from one snippet
Deploying to many accounts at once
Managing a service with no resource type
versions.explanation: Almost every AWS service is supported; custom resources cover the rest.

versions.question: Which value is the best fit for a template parameter?
options: The AMI ID for each Region you support
The instance size a team picks
The account ID the stack runs in
A port number fixed for all stacks
versions.explanation: Parameters suit values that change or aren't known ahead of time.
option_explanations: Known in advance: use a mapping.
Correct. It depends on the deployer.

versions.question: Why make a not-yet-known value a parameter instead of hardcoding it?
options: Parameters are visible to all other stacks
Changing it doesn't need a new template
versions.explanation: Parameters make templates reusable across teams.

versions.question: A parameter block in a template may include which properties? (Choose 3)
versions.explanation: Parameter constraints catch bad input before deployment.

versions.question: A parameter must accept only values matching a regex. Which property does that?
versions.explanation: Combine AllowedPattern with ConstraintDescription for a clear error.
option_explanations: The error message shown when a constraint fails.

versions.question: How do you make a parameter appear as a dropdown of fixed choices in the console?
options: Add a mapping of the choices
versions.explanation: AllowedValues gives users a choice while you keep control.
option_explanations: Accepts a list of values typed in.

versions.question: An InstanceType parameter defaults to t3.micro. How does an EC2 resource use it?
versions.explanation: !Ref on a parameter returns its value.

versions.question: Which parameter property shows a secret value as asterisks in the console and API output?
versions.explanation: NoEcho doesn't hide values you copy into Metadata or Outputs.

versions.question: Besides NoEcho, what's the stronger way to supply a database password to a template?
options: A Default value on the parameter
A mapping keyed by environment name
An export from a secrets stack
versions.explanation: Dynamic references resolve the secret at deploy time without storing it in the template.
option_explanations: Puts the secret in the template.
Correct. Or an SSM SecureString reference.

versions.question: `!Ref MyInstance` points at an AWS::EC2::Instance resource. What does it return?
versions.explanation: On a resource, !Ref returns its physical ID.
option_explanations: !Ref resolves to a value, not the name.

versions.question: `!Ref EnvType` points at a parameter. What comes back?
versions.explanation: Parameters and resources can't share a logical name, since !Ref works on both.
option_explanations: Resolves to a value, not the name.

versions.question: Which pseudo parameter returns the 12-digit number of the account the stack runs in?
versions.explanation: Pseudo parameters are always available with no setup.

versions.question: A template must build a bucket name that includes the current Region, with no user input. What should it reference?
versions.explanation: Others: AWS::StackId, AWS::StackName, AWS::NotificationARNs, AWS::NoValue.

versions.question: Which pseudo parameter, returned from !If, drops a property entirely?
versions.explanation: Typical use: !If [Cond, value, !Ref AWS::NoValue].

versions.question: What does `!Ref AWS::Region` return?
versions.explanation: Pseudo parameters replace values CloudFormation already knows.

versions.question: AMI IDs differ per Region and are all known when the template is written. Where should they live?
versions.explanation: Mappings suit values derived from Region, AZ, account or environment.

versions.question: Which intrinsic function reads a value from a template's Mappings section?
versions.explanation: Pair it with AWS::Region to pick per-Region values.
option_explanations: Picks an item from a list.

versions.question: A RegionMap mapping has Regions as top-level keys and HVM64 under each. Which picks the AMI for the stack's Region?
versions.explanation: Order: map name, top-level key, second-level key.
option_explanations: Keys are Regions, not stack names.
!Select picks an item from a list.

versions.question: In `!FindInMap [MapName, TopLevelKey, SecondLevelKey]` for a per-Region AMI map, what usually fills TopLevelKey?
versions.explanation: That makes one template work in every Region listed in the map.

versions.question: Instance size is chosen by whoever deploys the stack. Parameter or mapping?
versions.explanation: AMI per Region → mapping; size the user picks → parameter.

versions.question: Which describes when a mapping beats a parameter?
options: The value is a secret password
Every value is known in advance
versions.explanation: Mappings: known in advance. Parameters: depend on the user at deploy time.
option_explanations: Use NoEcho or a dynamic reference.

versions.question: How does an app stack read a VPC ID that a network stack exports?
versions.explanation: Exports plus !ImportValue make cross-stack references.
option_explanations: Reads attributes in the same stack.

versions.question: Two stacks need to share a subnet ID created in one of them. Which pairing works?
versions.explanation: Outputs can also simply be viewed in the console or CLI.
option_explanations: Needs a user to copy the value.

versions.question: Which are limits of CloudFormation cross-stack exports? (Choose 2)
options: Each account can hold just one export
An export can't be imported in another Region
A stack can't be deleted while its export is imported
Imports must be refreshed by hand after a change
versions.explanation: Import with !ImportValue ExportName.
option_explanations: Many exports are allowed; names must be unique per Region.
An export in use can't be changed at all.

versions.question: Stack B imports an export from stack A. What happens if you try to delete stack A?
versions.explanation: Exports in use can't be changed or removed.
option_explanations: Stacks aren't deleted in a chain.
The delete doesn't proceed at all.

versions.question: In stack A's Outputs, which key sets the name other stacks import a value by?
versions.explanation: Other stacks use !ImportValue with that export name.
option_explanations: Names the output inside the stack only.

versions.question: Stack A exports `CompanySshSG`. How does an instance in stack B list it in SecurityGroupIds?
versions.explanation: !Ref on a security group in stack A returns the ID that gets exported.

versions.question: An Auto Scaling policy should exist only in prod stacks, based on an EnvType parameter. What do you attach to it?
versions.explanation: Conditions can use Fn::And, Equals, If, Not and Or.

versions.question: Which defines an IsProd condition from an EnvType parameter?
versions.explanation: Conditions can reference parameters, mappings and other conditions.
option_explanations: !If picks values using a condition that already exists.
